summary: The @gyomu/schema package provides a robust foundational framework for modeling domain entities, enforcing structural validation, and managing operational errors. It serves as the primary source of truth for schema definitions, enabling consistent CRUD generation, complex data conversion, and standardized system-wide diagnostic patterns.
responsibilities: Define and maintain formal schemas for core business domain entities.
Centralize the application's error classification, context management, and operational policy logic.
Provide advanced tooling for TypeScript meta-programming, including symbol analysis, dependency tracking, and structural type modeling.
Establish standardized result patterns and JSON serialization protocols for predictable public API communication.
Enable automated CRUD schema suite generation for domain-driven development.

capabilities.name: Domain Entity Modeling
capabilities.description: Comprehensive tools for defining complex business entities, supporting automated CRUD schema generation and structured UI annotations.

capabilities.name: Centralized Error Infrastructure
capabilities.description: Consistent error classification and diagnostic context management that powers automated logging and retry logic across the system.

capabilities.name: TypeScript Code Analysis
capabilities.description: Framework for introspecting TypeScript structures, including symbol analysis, JSDoc parsing, and module-level dependency mapping.

capabilities.name: Standardized Data Validation
capabilities.description: Foundational validation patterns that ensure data integrity and provide developer-friendly diagnostic messages for complex schema failures.

capabilities.name: Public API Contract Management
capabilities.description: Utilities for wrapping internal logic into result-based schemas with predictable success and failure responses.

designDecisions: Utilizes Effect-based schemas to provide type-safe, composable, and runtime-validated data structures.
Employs a branded type strategy for critical identifiers to improve safety in domain-specific logic.
Adopts a trait-based error model, separating behavioral metadata (e.g., retryability) from the structural context of the error.
Centralizes schema definitions to act as a single source of truth for both static TypeScript types and runtime validation.
usageGuidance: Define all new domain entities within the entity registry to leverage automated CRUD schema generation.
Always extend the provided base error classes and context interfaces to ensure diagnostic metadata is preserved throughout the application.
Use the schema conversion utilities for boundary operations, such as handling external JSON input or persistence layer data, to guarantee runtime type safety.
Leverage the provided exhaustive type-checking utilities when handling unions to prevent unhandled state scenarios at compile time.
